etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Clipping of アクセラレータ (akuserarēta), from English accelerator.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English axel.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English up.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English decoration.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English base.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English bass.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English BACE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English maker.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 再 (“re-”) + 会 (“meeting”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 助 (“to help”) + 動詞 (“verb”), literally “helping verb”

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/keputei/ → /kefuteː/ → /keuteː/ → /kjoːteː/
Ultimately traceable back to Middle Chinese 協定 (MC hep dengH). However, this might be a much more recent term in Japanese, attested only since 1877, suggesting that this word may have been adopted as part of the modernization and internationalization efforts of the Meiji era (1868–1912).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Sinitic 臺本／台本 (táiběn).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連 is a daiyōji replacing 聯.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
夕(ゆう) (yū, “evening”) + 暮(く)れ (kure, “dusk, nightfall”).
The kure changes to gure as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 大(おお) (ō-, “big”) + 筋(すじ) (suji, “thread”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Derived from Middle Chinese 封 (MC pjowng|pjowngH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese tuki₂. Found in the Man'yōshū, completed some time after 759 CE, spelled phonetically in man'yōgana as 都奇, and in the Nihonshoki kayō (completed 720 CE) under the phonetic man'yōgana 豆紀.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 心 (shin, “heart”) + 情 (jō, “emotion”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 心 (kokoro, “attention, mind”) + 掛ける (kakeru, “latch onto”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From 心 (kokoro, “heart, feelings”) + 細い (hosoi, “slender”).
The hosoi changes to bosoi as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
怪(かい) (kai, “mysterious”) + 獣(じゅう) (jū, “beast”)
Comparable terms in other languages: Swedish vidunder, odjur

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Ultimately from Proto-Japonic *pantuy.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 意気(いき) (iki, “spirits, enthusiasm”) + 込(こ)む (komu, “to go into; to be full of, to have a lot of”). The komu changes to gomu as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From classical shimo nidan katsuyō verb 据う (suu), possibly parsed as *suwu. In the Muromachi period, there also exists a classical verb 据ゆ (suyu).
Compare 座る (suwaru, “sit”, intransitive).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 教 (kyō, “to teach”) + 科 (ka, “section; department”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *deh₃-
Proto-Indo-European *-r̥
Proto-Indo-European *dóh₃r̥ ~ *déh₃n̥s
Proto-Indo-European *-om
Proto-Indo-European *déh₃nom
Proto-Indo-Iranian *dáHnam
Sanskrit दान (dāna)bor.
Middle Chinese 旦那bor.
▲
Sanskrit दान (dāna)bor.
Middle Chinese 檀那bor.
Japanese 旦那
From Middle Chinese 旦那 (MC tanH na), 檀那 (MC dan na), both used as transliterations of Sanskrit दान (dā́na, “generosity, giving, donating”). Ultimately cognate with English donate and donor, from Proto-Indo-European *déh₃nom.
Attested in Japanese sinophone sources since at least the 1000s and in vernacular Japanese sources since at least 1287.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 望(のぞ)ま (nozoma, 未(み)然(ぜん)形(けい) (mizenkei, “irrealis form”) of the verb 望(のぞ)む (nozomu, “to wish, to hope, to want, to desire”)) + しい (-shī, adjective-forming suffix).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Likely from Middle Chinese compound 概略 (gə̀i lɨɐk̚, literally “generally, approximately + brief, abbreviated”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from verb 演(えん)ずる (enzuru), by natural progression from サ行変格活用 (sa-gyō henkaku katsuyō, “s-irregular conjugation”) verbs ending in -uru to 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 甲 (kæp).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 木 (Ki, “Wood”, one of the Five Elements) + の (no, attributive marker) + 兄 (e, “elder brother”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 迅速 (MC swinH suwk).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 金 (kana, “metal”) + 槌 (tsuchi, “hammer, mallet”). The tsuchi changes to zuchi as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: By surface analysis, 長 (chō, “chief, leader”) + 官 (kan, “government official”). Either a wasei kango from these on'yomi readings, or from Middle Chinese 長官 (sum-of-parts reading: /ɖɨɐŋ kuɑn/).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 上(かみ) (kami, “upper, person above”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from kami.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from kami. Also compare 神(こう)々(ごう)しい (kōgōshii), a shift from kamigamishii, in which the same kami component also shifts to kō.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 麻 is a daiyōji replacing 痲.
